entries.name: customers
entries.for: Example bizkernel module in Rust: customers whose name and email are personal data (ADR 28)

help.guide:
FOR
  Customers of a shop whose name and email are personal data. A customer
  (aggregate customer) is one person, identified by a customer_id the caller
  makes up. Name and email, and the greeting, are sealed with that
  customer's key: the module's own code only ever sees tokens.

FLOWS
  Sign-up: customer.register writes CustomerRegistered (name, email, tier
  gold or silver); the read model then lists the customer.
  Greeting: customer.greet on a registered customer writes CustomerGreeted
  (a fixed greeting, sealed like the other personal fields).
  A person or an agent applies both; no process or worker is involved.

BUILDING ON IT
  Read the view customers.list (table customers, one row per customer,
  filter by tier) to find customers; name and email come back opened by the
  kernel for those allowed to see them. Another module that needs to know
  a customer exists reads that view, or may start a process on
  CustomerRegistered or CustomerGreeted of aggregate customer. No settings,
  tasks or grants to set first.

TRIPS
  Make up a new uuid as customer_id for each customer; registering an id
  twice is rejected (customer_exists). customer.greet before register is
  rejected (no_customer): register first.
  tier is not personal and stays in the clear; only the two tiers exist.
  Name is 1 to 40 characters, email at least 3.

tier.description: not personal: kept in the clear

entries.name: devices
entries.for: Example bizkernel module in Rust: devices report what they measure through an intake (the MQTT intake, ADR 40)

help.guide:
FOR
  Devices (aggregate device) that report what they measure. A device is one
  sensor, identified by a device_id the caller makes up; its state is its
  last temperature and when it was reported, how many reports it made, and
  its last photo.

FLOWS
  Telemetry: an intake (the MQTT intake worker, subscribed to
  devices/+/telemetry) applies device.report for each message; it writes
  DeviceReported. The device_id is the topic's second level.
  Photo: the photo is uploaded first as a file (bk file put, or an intake's
  put_file), then device.photograph keeps it and writes DevicePhotographed.
  A person, an agent or an intake applies both commands; no process, task
  or view is declared.

BUILDING ON IT
  The module has no read model, process-start events or tasks: another
  module reads a device with bk state device <device_id> (temp, at,
  reports, photo, photos). An intake needs the broker allowed and its
  secret (devices/MQTT_PASSWORD) set when the worker is installed.

TRIPS
  device.report rejects a temp outside -100 to 200 (implausible_reading):
  fix the sensor or the unit, the value is never clamped.
  A second report replaces the temperature; only the last stays in state,
  though every report remains an event.
  A report delivered twice by the broker is one report only if the intake
  gives both the same key; applying by hand twice without a key writes two.
  The photo must be an image file already uploaded: pass the file as bk
  file put answered, not a path.

commands.name: device.report

entries.name: im
entries.for: The im module: a person's instant-messaging history imported for agents to read (CONTEXT: IM)

help.guide:
FOR
  A person's instant-messaging history, imported so that agents can read it.
  An intake reads each account's chats on a platform (wechat) and applies
  this module's commands; people and agents read it back. The nouns are
  four aggregates: account (who the history is read as), contact (a person
  as an account sees them), chat (one-to-one or group, with its members and
  notice) and message (one sent in a chat, of one kind, with its media).
  Every row is one account's: it holds what that account saw.

FLOWS
  Import: an intake applies contact.record, chat.record, then
  message.record for each message, and account.read to note how far it
  read. Applying the same thing again records nothing, so an intake
  may send everything each run; only what changed becomes an event.
  Names keep their history: bk history contact|account|chat <id> lists
  every earlier name, remark, member name and notice.
  Media: the intake uploads each file (bk file put) and sends its id in
  message.record. A media message recorded without its file is missing;
  message.attach (or message.record again with the file) adds it later.
  Voice, after a voice message is recorded with its file (or its missing
  file is found), TranscodeRequested and TranscribeRequested follow,
  each once per message, and start two separate processes:
    transcoding: queues task voice.transcode; the worker voice-transcode
      answers an Ogg Opus copy; the process applies
      message.record_transcode (VoiceTranscoded).
    transcribing: queues task voice.transcribe; the worker im-transcribe
      answers text, model and version; the process applies
      message.record_transcription (VoiceTranscribed, by worker).
  Neither waits for the other, and each fails alone. An intake may record
  the platform's own transcription with message.record_transcription.
  Again: message.transcode and message.transcribe ask a voice to be done
  again, as after a new worker or model is installed.

BUILDING ON IT
  Read with the view im.transcript (a chat's messages as one account saw
  them, in the platform's time order, each with its sender's display name
  and a quoted message attached; page with the returned next), or query
  the tables im.chats, im.contacts, im.members, im.messages. All carry
  platform and account columns: always filter by both.
  A process of yours may start on message MessageRecorded (a message was
  recorded), VoiceTranscoded or VoiceTranscribed (its copy or text is
  there now). Only an intake applies the import commands.
  Workers: install voice-transcode and im-transcribe, or no voice ever
  gets its copy or text (the processes wait for their tasks). Inspect a
  stuck voice with bk state transcoding|transcribing <id>, the id being
  the Requested event's.
  Grants to add (bk describe lists them under im's grants): owner for each
  person, naming their email, the platform and the accounts they own (view
  of those rows only); intake for the intake worker (apply on the
  commands, no view); transcode and transcribe for the two workers (work
  on their task). An agent reading for its person: bk auth delegate --scope
  im.transcript, which allows that view alone, no bk query.

TRIPS
  Senders are contact ids, never names. A one-to-one chat is named by its
  two contact ids sorted and joined by a comma, so both accounts name it
  the same. Name a group or message as the platform does; the same one
  seen from two accounts is one stream.
  message.record is refused (kind_mismatch) when a kind carries another
  kind's field or lacks its own, or a media field sits on a non-media kind;
  the fix names the field. Text and unknown carry no field.
  A file once recorded is kept: sending another records nothing.
  message.attach, transcode and transcribe on a message the account has not
  recorded: unknown_message; on a non-media or non-voice message: not_media
  or not_voice; on a voice recorded missing: missing, so attach first.
  Unsupported format or undecodable voice fails its process, not retried
  (it would fail again); the message stays as it was.
  The intake is granted no view: it cannot read back what it wrote.
  Give each message.record its own new --key uuid.

entries.name: invoices
entries.for: Example bizkernel module in Rust: an invoice takes a scan, which its row holds in a file column, so whoever may see the row may download it (ADR 75)

help.guide:
FOR
  Invoices (aggregate invoice) that take a scan, a file. An invoice is
  identified by an invoice_id the caller makes up; its state is how many
  scans it took.

FLOWS
  Attach: upload the scan first (bk file put answers the file), then
  invoice.attach writes ScanAttached. The read model puts the scan and the
  person who attached it into table scans. A person or an agent applies it.

BUILDING ON IT
  Read the view invoice.scans (table scans, filter by invoice_id) to get an
  invoice's scan and attached_by. attached_by is the person: who an agent
  acted for, else who applied the command. The scan column is a file
  column, so whoever may see the row by a grant whose condition reads
  attached_by may also download the scan. No processes, tasks or settings
  to set first. Add a recommended grant of your own for the people who may
  read scans; the module declares none.

TRIPS
  The scan must be a PDF or an image of at most 1 MiB; a larger or other
  file is rejected before the command runs.
  Attaching again to the same invoice adds a second scan event, but the
  scans table keeps one row per invoice, the latest scan and its attacher.

entries.name: loyalty
entries.for: Example bizkernel module in Rust: members earn and redeem points

help.guide:
FOR
  Loyalty points. A member's points account (aggregate points) is
  identified by a member_id the caller makes up; it holds a balance, the
  total earned and redeemed, and holds: points set aside for a while that
  no redeeming or other hold may take. The balance never goes below zero.

FLOWS
  Earn: points.earn credits points for a reason (e.g. the order id) and
  writes PointsEarned. Anyone applies it, including a worker or an agent.
  Redeem: points.redeem spends points on a reward and writes
  PointsRedeemed. Only the member applies it, signed in as themself; an
  agent is refused.
  Hold: points.hold sets points aside for some minutes (at most a week)
  and writes PointsHeld, plus a scheduled points.expire for the deadline.
  Then either points.release gives them back now (HoldReleased), or the
  kernel runs points.expire when the time is up (HoldExpired). Expire
  does nothing if the hold is gone or was held again until later.
  Transfer: start the process transfer (bk apply transfer.start) with
  transfer_id, from, to and points. Steps: redeem from the sender
  (points.redeem), earn for the receiver (points.earn); if the receiver
  is refused, a refund earns the points back for the sender. It ends
  completed, failed (nothing moved, or given back), or stuck when even
  the refund was refused: then credit the points by hand.

BUILDING ON IT
  Read the view points.accounts (table accounts: member_id, balance,
  earned, redeemed, updated_at), highest balance first; filter by member_id
  or a balance range. It does not show holds: the balance there includes
  held points, so the points available are in the account's state (bk
  state points <member_id>), balance less holds.
  Another module credits points by applying points.earn from its process,
  with a reason such as its order id. It may start on PointsEarned,
  PointsRedeemed, PointsHeld, HoldReleased or HoldExpired of aggregate
  points. No tasks, settings or grants are declared.

TRIPS
  Redeem and hold are limited by the balance not held, not the balance:
  insufficient_points names what is available. Redeeming by an agent is
  wrong_actor.
  A reason is required to earn (missing_reason); points are at least 1.
  Holding with an existing hold_id replaces that hold, its points and its
  deadline; use a new uuid for a second hold. Releasing a hold that is
  gone is rejected (not_held).
  Starting transfer again with the same input resumes it; a new transfer
  needs a new transfer_id.

entries.name: order
entries.for: Example bizkernel module in Rust: a pick-up order, from placed to captured, cancelled or refunded

help.guide:
FOR
  A pick-up order (mobile order and pay) at a store: a customer places it,
  its lines priced from the store's catalogue, the payment provider
  authorises its total, the store is sent it, and the payment is captured
  when it is picked up. The one aggregate is pickup_order: one order, a
  stream named pickup_order/<order_id>. Amounts are whole yen, tax included
  in the total. Each call out waits for an answer: succeeded, failed or
  unknown.

FLOWS
  Happy path (state names in brackets):
  1 pickup_order.place by the customer (an agent acts for them): reads the
    store's catalogue, records OrderPlaced with the lines as priced [placed].
  2 OrderPlaced starts process pickup_authorisation: it applies
    pickup_order.authorise, calls action payment.authorise, then applies
    pickup_order.answer [authorising, authorised]. If the provider answers
    with a redirect, the process waits for the provider's callback, applied
    as pickup_order.call_back; none in time fails the order and releases
    the payment (payment.release), even one paid by a late callback.
  3 Someone with the system role applies pickup_order.send [authorised ->
    sending to store]. SendStarted starts process sending, which queues task
    order.send_to_store (the hosted order-send worker posts it to the
    store, one order at a time per store) and applies pickup_order.answer
    [sent, send failed, or send unknown].
  4 At pick-up the payment system applies pickup_order.capture [sent ->
    capturing]. CaptureStarted starts process pickup_capture, which calls
    payment.capture and applies pickup_order.answer [captured].
  Cancel: pickup_order.cancel from authorised, sent, send failed or capture
  failed [deauthorising -> deauthorised]. Refund: an admin applies
  pickup_order.refund on a captured order [refunding -> refunded].
  No process in this module works cancelling or refunding: the system
  called applies pickup_order.answer itself.
  Unknown: a lost answer is first reconciled (the processes ask the
  provider with payment.find); a state still waiting when its time is up
  becomes unknown (pickup_order.time_out, run by the kernel). An admin
  settles an unknown one with pickup_order.confirm (it succeeded) or
  pickup_order.deny (it failed).

BUILDING ON IT
  Start your process on pickup_order OrderPlaced (a new order and its
  total), SendStarted, CaptureStarted, or the settled results
  CallAnswered, AnswerConfirmed, AnswerDenied, OrderCancelled.
  No views or tables: read an order with bk state pickup_order <id>.
  Apply: pickup_order.place (customer), authorise, send, capture, answer,
  call_back (systems), cancel (anyone but a timer), refund, confirm, deny
  (an admin; an agent is never one).
  Set up first: publish each store's catalogue (data.publish, data
  order.catalogue, key the store), set the store's key as secret
  order/STORE_KEY[<store>], install the order-send worker (or no send ever
  finishes: task order.send_to_store must be worked), point the actions
  payment.authorise, payment.capture, payment.find and payment.release at
  the provider's system (BIZKERNEL_ACTIONS), and make the provider's
  webhook apply pickup_order.call_back; the module declares no webhook.
  No recommended grants are declared; grant by the actors named above.

TRIPS
  Make up a new uuid order_id for each order; a reused one is refused
  (already_placed). Publish the store's catalogue before the first order
  (no_catalogue). The store is a key of ASCII letters, digits, - _ and .;
  its address an https URL. Items and components are named exactly as the
  catalogue names them (unknown_item, unknown_component); a sold-out item
  is refused (sold_out). A catalogue published later changes no placed
  order. A discount larger than its line only takes the line to 0; an
  order whose total is 0 is refused (nothing_to_pay).
  wrong_actor is the common rejection: each command has its own actor
  (above). not_now means the order is in another state; finished means it
  is in a state nothing leads out of (authorise failed, deauthorised,
  deauthorise failed, refunded, refund failed).
  capture and refund take an amount: left out, all that is authorised or
  captured; 0 is refused (no_amount), more is refused (more_than_authorised,
  more_than_captured).
  Authorise, capture and sending to a store are done at most once, never
  retried: a call without an answer ends unknown, for an admin.

entries.name: pick_one
entries.for: Puts a choice to a person: an agent offers options, each with its reason; the person picks one and may add a note
entries.guide:
FOR
  An agent that needs a person to choose: it offers the options, each with
  the reason for it, and gets back the one they picked and their note.

ASK
  Install it once, for yourself (bk app install --from-catalog pick_one),
  then ask in its route "choose":

    bk app ask pick_one --route choose --to <person> --wait --args '{
      "question": "Which carrier ships the Osaka order?",
      "options": [
        {"option": "Yamato", "reason": "arrives tomorrow, 1200 yen"},
        {"option": "Sagawa", "reason": "arrives in two days, 900 yen"}
      ]}'

  args: question, what is asked (a string); options, at least one, each
  an option (a string, unique among them) and the reason for it (a
  string, may be "").

ANSWER
  {"option": <the option picked, as it was given>, "note": <what the person
  added, "" when nothing>}: the kernel holds the answer to that shape.

TRIPS
  The person asked opens the link bk prints; nobody else may answer.
  Args not of this shape are shown to the person as what is wrong with
  them, and they cannot answer: ask again with args of this shape.

entries.name: questions
entries.for: Example bizkernel module in Rust: a process asks Claude through a hosted worker (a task, ADR 31, 33), whose answer streams to whoever watches, then records the answer

help.guide:
FOR
  Questions put to Claude, with the answers recorded. A question (aggregate
  question) is identified by a question_id the caller makes up; it is
  answered once, by one model.

FLOWS
  Ask: start the process answering (bk apply answering.start, with a new
  question_id as the key's stream) with a prompt.
  1. It queues a task of type claude.ask (step ask).
  2. A hosted worker, claude-ask, claims it, calls the Claude Messages API
     and streams the text to the task's output (bk task watch <task>
     shows it as it is written); it completes the task with the whole
     answer and the model.
  3. The process applies question.answer (step record), which writes
     QuestionAnswered; the process completes.
  If the ask fails for good the process fails with the worker's error; if
  the worker answers without an answer and model it is stuck for a person.
  question.answer can also be applied by hand.

BUILDING ON IT
  Another module's process may start answering through its own command and
  later read the question's state (answer, model) with bk state question
  <question_id>, or start on QuestionAnswered of aggregate question.
  The claude.ask task must be worked: install the claude-ask worker, or
  nothing finishes. Set its secret questions/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY first.
  Allow the worker to reach the API host; an api_url elsewhere needs its
  host allowed too.

TRIPS
  A second answer to the same question_id is rejected (already_answered):
  use a new id for a new question.
  Starting answering again with the same input resumes it rather than
  asking twice.
  A stop_reason of max_tokens means the answer was cut short; it is still
  recorded.
  model is optional in the input: left empty the worker chooses.

entries.name: reports
entries.for: Example bizkernel module in Rust: a process renders a report through a self-hosted worker (a task, ADR 31), then publishes it

help.guide:
FOR
  Reports rendered to a PDF by a worker that can run anywhere, then
  published or delivered. A report (aggregate report) is identified by a
  report_id the caller makes up; it ends published (with its PDF and page
  count) or abandoned (with why), never both.

FLOWS
  Publish: upload the data CSV (bk file put), then start the process
  publishing (bk apply publishing.start) with report_id, title, rows and
  data.
  1. It queues a task of type report.render (step render).
  2. A worker claims it, reads the data file, renders a PDF and completes
     the task with the PDF file and page count.
  3. The process applies report.publish (step publish), which writes
     ReportPublished; the process completes.
  If the render fails for good (its attempts or timeout run out, or the
  task is cancelled), the process applies report.abandon (step abandon),
  which writes ReportAbandoned, and fails.
  Deliver: start the process delivering with a delivery_id, a store and a
  title. It queues a task of type report.deliver ordered by the store; the
  worker answers the store's receipt and the process completes, or fails
  with why.

BUILDING ON IT
  No view or table is declared: read a report with bk state report
  <report_id> (report file, pages, abandoned). Another module's process may
  start on ReportPublished or ReportAbandoned of aggregate report: the
  first means the PDF is final, the second means it never will be.
  Workers must work both task types or nothing finishes: report.render
  (the example worker is self-hosted, report-render) and report.deliver.
  No settings or grants to set first.

TRIPS
  Publishing a published report is rejected (already_published), as is
  changing an abandoned one (already_abandoned): use a new report_id.
  Abandoning a published report is rejected too; published stays published.
  Rows and pages must be at least 1.
  Deliveries to one store run one at a time, in the order started, at
  most one a second; other stores' deliveries run beside them. A delivery
  is tried once and fails if the store refuses.
  Starting a process again with the same input resumes it; a new
  delivery_id is a new delivery.
